ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Question: 267
One of the students in the school council election wants to make healthy lunch menus her pitch to gain votes. What size voter sample would she need to obtain a 90% confidence that her support level margin of error is no more than 4%?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Use the standard sample-size formula for estimating a proportion with unknown support level. The confidence level is 90%, so use z = 1.645. The desired margin of error is E = 0.04. Since no prior estimate of the support proportion is given, use the conservative value p = 0.5, so p(1 - p) = 0.25. Solve n >= z^2 p(1-p) / E^2 = 1.645^2 * 0.25 / 0.04^2 = 422.8 approximately. Since sample size must be a whole number and the margin of error must be no more than 4%, round up to 423.

method.method_draft: Use the standard sample-size calculation for estimating an unknown voting proportion. From the question text, take confidence level 90% and required margin of error E = 0.04. Since no prior support proportion is given, use the conservative worst-case value p = 0.5, so p(1-p)=0.25. For 90% confidence use z = 1.645. Apply E = z * sqrt(p(1-p)/n), so n >= z^2 * 0.25 / 0.04^2 = about 422.8. Round up to the next whole voter, giving 423.
